title.en: A later manuscript of The City of Ladies

alt.en: An illuminated manuscript page has two columns of French text, red headings, floral borders, and a miniature of a seated woman reading beside three standing women.
alt.zh: 绘饰手稿页有两栏法文、红色标题和花卉边饰；小画中，一位女子坐着读书，身旁站着三位女子。

caption.en: France. A page from a manuscript combining works by Boccaccio and Christine de Pizan, Getty Ms. 129 (2024.156). Text, frames and initials date to about 1470; frames and miniatures were added about 1515–1520.
caption.zh: 法国。将薄伽丘与克里斯蒂娜·德·皮桑作品合编的手抄本中的一页，盖蒂藏Ms. 129（2024.156）。文字、边框和首字母约作于1470年；另一些边框及小画约于1515—1520年加入。

interpretation.en: The decorated page makes the circulation of Christine’s writing tangible: copying and illumination continued after her death. Its reader, books and female visitors put learned women at the centre of the image. This is a later manuscript illustration, not a portrait made during Christine’s lifetime.
interpretation.zh: 这页绘饰手稿使克里斯蒂娜作品的传播变得具体可见：她去世后，抄写与绘饰仍在继续。读者、书籍与女性来访者把有学识的女性置于画面中心。这是后世手抄本插画，并非克里斯蒂娜生前绘制的肖像。

title.en: Augustus and the image of imperial authority

alt.en: A pale marble portrait head on a dark support shows a clean-shaven man with short curved locks across his forehead against a gray background.
alt.zh: 灰色背景前，深色支架托起浅色大理石头像：男子面部无须，短发卷曲并覆在前额。

caption.en: Unknown Roman maker, Portrait Head of Augustus, 25–1 BCE. Marble; Getty 78.AA.261. The sculpture dates to Augustus’s lifetime and the early Principate.

interpretation.en: The youthful face and carefully arranged hair make rulership visible through an idealized portrait. Getty identifies this image as political representation rather than a literal record of Augustus’s age or appearance, directly illustrating how the Principate projected legitimacy.
interpretation.zh: 年轻面容与精心排列的发式，通过理想化肖像使统治权获得可见形式。盖蒂将其解释为政治形象，而非奥古斯都年龄或外貌的忠实记录，直接展示了元首制如何塑造合法性。

title.en: Christine de Pizan · Writing women into a learned world
title.zh: 克里斯蒂娜·德·皮桑 · 在知识世界书写女性

location.label: Paris; representative literary and courtly setting

labelI18n.en: Paris; representative literary and courtly setting
labelI18n.zh: 巴黎；文学与宫廷生活的代表性背景地点

summary.en:
Christine de Pizan made writing and book production a livelihood within the courtly world of late medieval France. Widowhood and responsibility for her household formed part of this history, alongside patronage, copying and illumination. Her works were material books made with collaborators and presented to readers who could support their production.

The Book of the City of Ladies answered hostile representations of women through an allegorical construction populated by exemplary figures. The Book of the Three Virtues offered instruction to women in different social positions. These projects should be read in their medieval moral and hierarchical setting rather than treated as a direct statement of every modern political position. Manuscript copies reveal circulation and adaptation, while gaps in the record make some biographical dates approximate. Her entry connects intellectual argument with the economic and collaborative work of making books before printing transformed their distribution.
summary.zh:
克里斯蒂娜·德·皮桑在法国中世纪晚期宫廷世界中，以写作和制作书籍维持生计。守寡、家庭责任，以及资助、抄写和绘饰共同构成这段历史。她的作品是与合作者制作的物质书籍，并呈献给能够支持制作的读者。

《女性之城》通过由典范人物组成的寓言城市，回应对女性的敌意描写。《三德之书》则向不同社会位置的女性提供教导。应把这些项目放回中世纪道德与等级环境，而非当作所有现代政治立场的直接表达。手抄本显示作品的流传与改写，史料空缺也使部分生平日期只能约定。她的条目把思想论辩与印刷改变传播方式之前的经济及协作劳动联系起来。

dateNote.en: Approximate lifespan c.1364–c.1430 follows BnF’s qualified authority dates; City of Ladies is dated 1404–1405.
dateNote.zh: 约1364年至约1430年的生平采用法国国家图书馆有保留的权威日期；《女性之城》约作于1404—1405年。

title.en: 800: Charlemagne and a new imperial claim

summary.en: Charlemagne’s coronation as emperor in Rome linked Frankish kingship with a revived claim to Roman imperial authority in western Europe. His realm already stretched across much of the continent, held together through conquest, aristocratic relationships and cooperation with the church. The court sponsored learning, manuscripts and buildings that adapted classical and Christian models. Aachen became a particularly important centre of this political culture. The coronation did not reunite all former Roman lands: an eastern Roman emperor still ruled from Constantinople. It created another powerful language of legitimacy within a divided medieval world.
summary.zh: 查理曼在罗马加冕为皇帝，使法兰克王权与西欧复兴罗马帝权的主张相结合。他的国家已横跨欧洲大片地区，依靠征服、贵族关系与教会合作维系。宫廷支持学术、抄本和建筑，改造古典与基督教传统，亚琛成为重要中心。加冕并未统一全部罗马故地，君士坦丁堡仍有东罗马皇帝；它在分裂的中世纪世界中建立了另一套强大的合法性语言。

dateNote.en: The coronation occurred in Rome on 25 December 800; Aachen is the representative court marker.
dateNote.zh: 800年12月25日在罗马加冕；地图以主要宫廷所在地亚琛为参照。

title.en: The Black Death: catastrophe and uneven change
title.zh: 黑死病：灾难与不均衡的变化

summary.en: The Black Death devastated communities across Europe and formed part of a wider pandemic affecting regions beyond it. Mortality disrupted households, work and religious life, but its consequences were not identical everywhere. Research on medieval Cambridge compares skeletal evidence before and after the epidemic and finds substantial continuity in everyday conditions alongside catastrophe. Written records and human remains answer different questions: institutions might change while many ordinary people continued to experience similar diets, labor demands and physical stresses.
summary.zh: 黑死病重创欧洲各地，并属于影响更广地区的大流行。大量死亡打乱家庭、劳动与宗教生活，但各地后果并不相同。对中世纪剑桥遗骸的研究比较疫情前后状况，发现灾难之外，日常生活条件仍有明显延续。文字档案和人体遗存回答不同问题，制度变化也可能与普通人生活的延续并存。

dateNote.en: 1347–1353 is a conventional span for the first major European wave; local outbreaks and later recurrences had different dates.
dateNote.zh: 1347—1353年为欧洲第一轮主要疫情的常用分期；地方暴发与后续疫情年代各异。

sources.title: More continuity than change following the Black Death epidemic in medieval Cambridge

title.en: Roman Principate: emperors within republican forms
title.zh: 罗马元首制：共和形式下的皇帝

labelI18n.zh: 罗马；政治背景参考位置

summary.en:
Augustus assembled durable personal power after the republic’s civil wars while retaining institutions such as the Senate. The resulting Principate was a political arrangement, not simply another name for the city of Rome. Emperors relied on armies, provincial administration, taxation and relationships with local elites across the Mediterranean. Imperial portraits and public buildings helped make this authority visible.

Provisioning cities and maintaining roads, ports and military settlements connected government to work and commerce. Provincial communities participated on unequal terms, and slavery remained part of the imperial economy. This overview connects the republic with the later imperial reorganization rather than treating every emperor as a separate timeline row. The selected endpoint marks Diocletian’s accession and a change of governing framework; it does not mean Roman institutions or provincial societies disappeared in 284.
summary.zh:
共和末期内战之后，奥古斯都在保留元老院等制度的同时，建立了持久的个人权力。由此形成的元首制是一种政治安排，并非罗马城的另一个名称。皇帝依靠军队、行省行政、税收和地方精英之间的关系治理地中海世界；皇帝肖像和公共建筑让权威获得可见形式。

城市供给以及道路、港口、军事聚落的维持，把政府与劳动和商业联系起来。行省群体参与帝国的条件并不平等，奴隶劳动也是帝国经济的一部分。本条把共和国与后来的帝国重组连接起来，不为每位皇帝设置年表行。284年是戴克里先即位及统治框架转变的节点，不表示罗马制度和行省社会在这一年消失。

dateNote.en: Focus: 27 BCE–284 CE, a conventional political phase; representative Rome point, not territorial extent.
dateNote.zh: 关注公元前27年至公元284年的传统政治分期；罗马点位不表示疆域。

title.en: After Alexander: a world of competing kingdoms
title.zh: 亚历山大之后：诸王国的世界

summary.en: After Alexander’s death, his generals and their successors divided his conquests into rival kingdoms. The Antigonids, Seleucids and Ptolemies governed different societies, while some Greek cities organized leagues to protect their independence. Courts supported monumental art, libraries and luxury production; mobile craftspeople and merchants carried techniques between regions. Greek cultural forms spread through unequal encounters with older local traditions, producing varied societies rather than a single uniform civilization. Roman expansion gradually absorbed these kingdoms. Pella marks the Macedonian connection, while the history itself extended across the eastern Mediterranean and deep into Asia.
summary.zh: 亚历山大去世后，将领及其继承者把征服地区分为竞争的王国。安提柯、塞琉古和托勒密王朝治理不同社会，部分希腊城邦则通过联盟维护独立。宫廷支持大型艺术、图书馆与奢侈品制作，工匠和商人流动传播技术。希腊文化与更古老的地方传统在不平等接触中融合，形成多样社会，并非统一文明。罗马逐渐兼并这些国家；佩拉仅代表马其顿起点。

dateNote.en: 323–31 BCE follows the Met’s period convention, ending at Actium; Egypt’s formal annexation followed in 30 BCE.
dateNote.zh: 前323—31年采用博物馆分期，以亚克兴海战为末；埃及正式并入罗马在前30年。

christine.name: Des cleres et nobles femmes; Le livre de la Cité des Dames
christine.description:
The text of this French copy of Giovanni Boccaccio’s Concerning Famous and Noble Women (composed 1361–62) and Christine de Pizan’s The Book of the City of Ladies (composed around 1404–5) was first written out in the late fifteenth-century, but its 108 images were not added until the early sixteenth century. Spaces were originally  left throughout the manuscript for images and decorated initials, meaning that the volume was always intended to be decorated. Both works feature biographies of famous women from Antiquity through the medieval period, though Boccaccio’s text cements sexist tropes while Christine’s subverts them. One of two known manuscripts to bring these two texts together, this volume contributes to an understanding of the late medieval “dispute of women” (querelle des dames), a literary debate on women’s roles in society.
The identical layout of both sections of text indicates a clear and insightful intention to associate the two works in a single volume. A complete cycle of illustration, added by two of the premier Parisian illuminators of the day, Étienne Colaud (active c. 1512–41) and the Master of the François de Rohan (active c. 1520–46), features one-column miniatures that introduce each of the one hundred and five chapters of Famous Women and each of the three sections of the City of Ladies. The roles of women as painters, sculptors, weavers, writers, and musicians—as well as queens, warriors, consorts, and mothers—are particularly emphasized in the image program.
Although many of the narratives purport to take place in the ancient past, all figures and scenes are depicted as contemporary to the sixteenth century, complete with up-to-date clothing and Renaissance architectural spaces. Even warrior queens like the Amazonian Marpesia are rendered in medieval knightly armor rather than ancient Greek breastplates and helmets. The high technical quality of the illumination and diversity of the iconographic program in the manuscript attest to the wealth and taste of the codex’s original patrons and to the ingenuity and skill of its artists.
christine.material: Tempera colors, gold and silver paint, and ink

charlemagne.name: The Coronation of Charlemagne
charlemagne.description: Charlemagne laid the foundations of the Holy Roman Empire, the league of central European, mostly German-speaking lands that lasted for a millennium. This grand, multifigured composition celebrates one of the great events of German history, when Pope Leo III crowned Charlemagne the first Holy Roman Emperor in Rome in the year 800. The drawing was preparatory for a fresco, commissioned by Ludwig I, king of Bavaria, for the royal palace in Munich. The subject emphasized the religious and political bonds between Italy and Catholic Germany.

plague.name: Blessed Bernard Tolomei Interceding for the Cessation of the Plague in Siena
plague.description:
During the Black Death of 1348, the Blessed Bernard Tolomei left the safety of his Benedictine monastery in Monte Oliveto and returned to his native Siena to attend to the sick and dying. He succumbed to the plague that same year and soon became the object of religious devotion. An abbot from Bernard's monastic order commissioned this painting in 1736, when Bernard was being considered for sainthood. Giuseppe Maria Crespi interpreted the story's pathos with great depth, expression, and immediacy.   
 Wearing a white robe and holding a crucifix, Bernard and a fellow monk attend to plague victims in an open-air encampment outside the walls of Siena. On the left, a priest walks under an umbrella, accompanied by an acolyte. Several plague-stricken figures languish on the ground in various stages of death. Below Bernard, a woman slumps over while her small child desperately tries to pull her upright. At her feet, the foreshortened body of a dead infant falls in the area between the acolyte and bowing monk. A woman has perished in the right corner, her gray-skinned body lifeless, thus a man above her holds a cloth over his mouth to avoid smelling the stench. Contorted, highlighted figures emerge from the shadowy darkness to confront the viewer, accordingly heightening the emotion of the drama.

augustus.name: Portrait Head of Augustus
augustus.description:
After many years of civil war, Augustus took complete power in Rome in 27 B.C. He claimed that he was re-establishing the Roman Republic, but he actually founded the Roman Empire. Visual signs emphasizing its power and legitimacy bolstered this new political order.   
 Portraits of Augustus served as symbols of his political agenda rather than corresponding to his physical features as described in written sources. Augustus is always shown in an ideal, classicizing style, and his appearance bears little relation to his actual age. One constant feature of Augustus's portraits is his hairstyle, with its distinctive forked locks of hair on his forehead.

# Getty images 02: four focused additions and one size repair

Reviewed 2026-11-11. Getty-only curation against full `loadAtlasRecords()` records and `dist/data/visual-coverage-v18.json` coveredIds. No production files, Git operations, uploads, deployments, or Actions changed.

## Integration-ready files

- `research/v18/getty-images-02/visual-assets-getty-images-02-v18.json`: four new bilingual records with explicit associations, rights, localized metadata, hashes and dimensions.
- JPEGs in the same folder: `charlemagne.jpg`, `plague.jpg`, `augustus.jpg`, `berenike.jpg`. The proposed catalog filenames include the `getty-images-02-` prefix; rename on integration.
- `christine-replacement-v18.json`: replace the previous Christine item rather than adding a duplicate. Its original asset ID and proposed production filename remain unchanged. Copy `christine.jpg` to that production filename. Corrected kind to `manuscript` with `manuscript-detail` representation.
- `download-receipts.json`: source URLs, HTTP 200 receipts, dimensions, bytes, SHA-256 and actual-pixel inspection records.
- `audit.json`: both catalogs passed `auditHistoryMedia` with zero errors against the current full records.

## Focal matches and limits

1. `charlemagne-coronation`: [The Coronation of Charlemagne](https://www.getty.edu/art/collection/object/109DCT), Julius Schnorr von Carolsfeld, 1840, Getty 2009.5. 1024 × 568; 250724 bytes. Direct depiction of the 800 coronation, explicitly a nineteenth-century Bavarian royal commission, not eyewitness evidence or a lifetime portrait. Its central crowning gesture and surrounding ranks are visible.
2. `black-death`: [Blessed Bernard Tolomei Interceding for the Cessation of the Plague in Siena](https://www.getty.edu/art/collection/object/103RHC), Giuseppe Maria Crespi, about 1735, Getty 86.PC.463. 1400 × 905; 247497 bytes. Explicit later devotional treatment of the 1348 Black Death in Siena, not evidence for the record’s Cambridge skeletal study. Painting includes sick and deceased people, including children; non-graphic historical depiction. Getty’s date field says about 1735 while its descriptive text mentions a 1736 commission; retain the catalogue’s approximate date, not an asserted exact production year.
3. `roman-principate`: [Portrait Head of Augustus](https://www.getty.edu/art/collection/object/103THA), unknown maker, 25–1 BCE, Getty 78.AA.261. 1157 × 1400; 162947 bytes. This lifetime-period marble portrait directly supports the record’s discussion of imperial portraits and legitimacy. The text makes clear that the idealized face is political imagery, not literal age or appearance.
4. `hellenistic-kingdoms`: [Oval intaglio](https://www.getty.edu/art/collection/object/103V11), unknown maker, 3rd–2nd century BCE, Getty 81.AN.76.207. 1050 × 1400; 147635 bytes. Getty specifically identifies Berenike II of Ptolemaic Egypt. It is a particular royal-image object connected to the record’s Ptolemaic court and luxury-production discussion, not generic period padding. The broad date spans after her lifetime; no securely dated lifetime likeness claimed.
5. Existing Christine repair: 961 × 1400; 530443 bytes. Same verified official source image and content as world-batch-16; source-served smaller derivative solves the 750000-byte ceiling without changing policy or local image pixels.

Each object page returned HTTP 200 and includes image-specific CC0 evidence plus the exact IIIF identity in JSON-LD `thumbnailUrl`. Saved HTML and schema files preserve that evidence for the four new records. Christine’s original rights evidence remains in `research/v18/world-batch-16`. All five files were opened with `view_image`; focal subjects, intact framing, absence of watermark/error pages and unchanged pixels were checked. Every accepted image is within the unchanged 3000px and 750000-byte limits.

## Source behavior and exclusions

Requests were sequential with pauses. No 403 or challenge occurred. Charlemagne’s `!1400,1400` and then `!1024,1024` requests returned HTTP 400. The public IIIF info document identifies a native 1024 × 568 source; the standard `/full/max/0/default.jpg` endpoint returned 200, preserving native dimensions. This was a size-syntax correction, not an access-denial workaround.

No other image providers were probed or downloaded. Other search leads such as generic Constantinople photographs, a later Bastille square photograph, and an uncertain Jerusalem destruction manuscript were not admitted: they did not yet establish sufficiently specific focal relevance. Four strong additions were preferred over filling the twelve-item ceiling with weak matches.
